title: boop. — A little push. A clever game.
voice: A warm adult woman with a clear, rounded mid-register voice, natural American English, a friendly smile and precise diction. Conversational board-game teacher, not an advertisement. Relaxed but lively, moderate pace, gentle emphasis on rule contrasts. No music or sound effects.

scenes.title:
A little push.
A clever game.
scenes.caption: 2 players   ·   About 20 minutes
scenes.text: Meet Boop: a cozy game with a surprisingly clever twist. Every piece you place gives its neighbors a little push. Turn your kittens into cats, then line up three cats to win.

scenes.title: Make the bed.
scenes.caption: 6 × 6 quilt   ·   8 kittens per player
scenes.text: Turn the box bottom upside down and lay the quilt on top. Each player starts with eight kittens of their color. Keep the eight adult cats off to the side, in reserve. Whoever most recently pet a cat goes first, or choose randomly.

scenes.title: Place one piece.
scenes.caption: Your color. An empty square.
scenes.text: On your turn, place one of your available pieces on any empty square. At first, you only have kittens. Later, you can choose a kitten or a cat from your pool. You do not move a piece that's already on the bed.

scenes.title: Neighbors go boop.
scenes.caption: All 8 directions   ·   Either color
scenes.text: The piece you place boops every adjacent piece that it can push, one square directly away. That includes diagonal neighbors, and pieces of either color. All these pushes happen as part of the same placement.

scenes.title:
Off the bed?
Back to the pool.
scenes.caption: Not captured. Ready for a later turn.
scenes.text: At the edge, a piece can be booped right off the bed. Return it to its owner's pool. It isn't captured, and it can be played again on a later turn. Sometimes, pushing your own piece off is useful.

scenes.title:
No room?
No push.
scenes.caption: An occupied destination blocks that boop.
scenes.text: If the square directly behind a neighbor is occupied, that neighbor stays put. Two pieces lined up together cannot be pushed into each other, whatever their colors. You can still boop them from another direction.

scenes.title:
One push.
No chain reaction.
scenes.caption: Only the newly placed piece causes boops.
scenes.text: A piece that gets booped does not boop anything else. Here, the kitten moves one square and stops. The next piece does not move. Boop is one ring of pushes, not a domino effect.

scenes.title:
Three in a row?
Time to graduate.
scenes.caption: Your pieces   ·   Across, down or diagonal
scenes.text: After the boops finish, check for three of your pieces in a row: across, down, or diagonally. A row of three kittens graduates. Remove those kittens from the bed, retire them from the game, and take three adult cats from your reserve.

scenes.title:
The cats go
to your pool.
scenes.caption: Not onto those three squares.
scenes.text: Put the new cats in your available pool, not onto the board. Those three squares are now empty. You always have eight active pieces in total, split between the bed and your pool. Graduation changes what those pieces are.

scenes.title:
Cats have
staying power.
scenes.caption: Kitten → kitten     Cat → either
scenes.text: Cats can boop both kittens and cats. But kittens cannot boop cats. That makes cats harder to dislodge. The occupied-square rule still applies: being a cat doesn't let you push a whole line.

scenes.title:
Mixed rows
count, too.
scenes.caption: Graduate the kittens. Return the cats.
scenes.text: A row of your pieces can mix kittens and cats. Remove all three pieces. Retire any kittens and replace them with cats from reserve. Existing cats simply return to your pool. If all three are cats, that's a win instead.

scenes.title:
All 8 pieces
on the bed.
scenes.caption: Choose one piece to bring back.
scenes.text: If all eight of your pieces are on the bed, you may remove one kitten, retire it, and put a reserve cat in your pool. Or, if it helps your position, return one of your existing cats to your pool instead.

scenes.title:
One graduation
at a time.
scenes.caption: Choose a group of 3, or the full-bed option.
scenes.text: If you make a longer row or several connected rows, choose one group of three to graduate. Leave the rest on the bed. If you also have all eight pieces out, choose either the row or the single-piece option, not both.

scenes.title:
Three cats.
One winner.
scenes.caption: Across, down or diagonal   ·   Your color
scenes.text: You win with three of your adult cats in a row: horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. Wait until every boop has finished before checking. Three cats that were together only before the pushes do not count.

scenes.title:
Eight cats
on the bed.
scenes.caption: All 8 of your adult cats, after the boops.
scenes.text: There's a second way to win: have all eight of your adult cats on the bed at the end of a turn. Eight mixed pieces can unlock the full-bed option, but only eight cats wins this way.

scenes.title:
Place. Boop.
Check.
scenes.caption: Make kittens into cats. Make cats into a win.
scenes.text: That's the rhythm: place one piece, resolve its boops, then check for a win or graduation. Watch the edges, protect your pairs, and remember that even your own pieces can get booped. Cute cats. Serious strategy.

scenes.title:
A simpler
first game.
scenes.caption: Kittens only   ·   First row of 3 wins
scenes.text: For a simpler game with younger players, leave the cats in the box and skip graduation. The first player to line up three kittens wins. When everyone's comfortable with the little push, bring the cats back in.
